title: Vishnupad Temple Gaya — Complete Pilgrim Guide, History & Darshan Timings
metaDescription: Complete pilgrim guide to Vishnupad Temple in Gaya — Lord Vishnu's 40cm footprint, temple architecture, darshan timings, puja booking, and Pind Daan procedures at the sanctum.
author: Acharya Pandit V. K. Gayawal
reviewedBy: Vishnupad Temple Trust & Gayawal Purohit Sabha
summary: Vishnupad Temple stands at the spiritual heart of Gaya, housing the divine 40cm footprint of Lord Vishnu imprinted on solid basalt rock. This complete pilgrim guide covers history, architecture, darshan timings, and ritual procedures.
content:
The Vishnupad Temple (Vishnu Pada Mandir) is the most sacred site in all of Gaya Kshetra and the spiritual epicentre of ancestral Pind Daan worship. The temple enshrines the divine paduka (footprint) of Lord Vishnu imprinted 40cm deep into solid basalt rock — making Gaya the only place on earth where Vishnu's physical presence is enshrined as Pitru Tarpana Peetha.

### Sacred Architecture & Temple Layout
The current temple structure was rebuilt in 1787 by Ahilya Bai Holkar, the Maratha queen renowned for her temple restoration projects across India. The octagonal shikhara tower rises 30 metres above the Falgu River ghats, and the outer mandap (hall) is encircled by 108 carved shrines representing the entire Gaya Kshetra circuit.

The innermost sanctum contains:
- **Vishnupad Stone**: The 40cm footprint basin filled with water considered equivalent to all sacred rivers
- **Pind Offering Altar**: Where Gayawal Purohits place ancestral Pinda on behalf of pilgrim families
- **Vamsavali Registry**: Ancient lineage records maintained by Gayawal families dating back 2,000 years

### Temple Darshan Timings
| Session | Time | Entry Type |
|---|---|---|
| Mangala Aarti | 4:00 AM – 4:30 AM | Advance booking |
| Morning Darshan | 5:00 AM – 12:00 PM | Open public |
| Afternoon Break | 12:00 PM – 4:00 PM | Closed |
| Evening Darshan | 4:00 PM – 9:00 PM | Open public |
| Shayan Aarti | 9:00 PM – 9:30 PM | Special pass |

sections.heading: Performing Pind Daan at Vishnupad Temple
sections.body: Pinda offered directly at the Vishnupad footprint stone is considered the most powerful of all the 45 Gaya Dhaams. Your assigned Gayawal Purohit will guide the Sankalp, Pinda creation, offering, and final prayers. Pitraya Rituals coordinates entry timing, puja samagri, and archival Vamsavali registration.

sections.heading: Photography & Entry Rules
sections.body: Photography is strictly prohibited inside the inner sanctum. Non-Hindu visitors are not permitted beyond the outer mandap. Traditional dress (dhoti-kurta for men, saree or salwar-kameez for women) is mandatory.

faqs.question: Can women perform Pind Daan at Vishnupad Temple?
faqs.answer: Yes. Daughters and female relatives can perform Pind Daan at Vishnupad Temple. There are no gender-based restrictions on performing ancestral rites.

faqs.question: How long does a Pind Daan ceremony at Vishnupad Temple take?
faqs.answer: A complete Pind Daan at Vishnupad Temple conducted by a Gayawal Purohit takes approximately 2-3 hours including Sankalp, Pinda preparation, offering, and Brahmin Bhojan.
